Subject: EdgeStream evaluation: reliability probes, baseline metrics, and next tests

Hi Ryan / Leah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the reliability comparison vs the hyperscaler incumbents:

Summary of what we heard
- You run critical inference for content personalization (low-latency online requests and periodic bulk scoring).
- Primary concerns: intermittent 5xx bursts, opaque rate limits from current provider, and unpredictable failover behavior when a region blips.
- Your procurement threshold: clear uptime SLA (99.95+), deterministic rate-limiting thresholds, and a reproducible failover test you can run with your platform team.

What Redwood can provide for the evaluation
- SLO matrix with our baseline targets (attached): uptime, p99/p50 latency for online + batch taillatency, and rate-limit behavior under concurrent connections.
- Failover probes that simulate node/regional loss and validate graceful degradation to fallback model variants.
- Side-by-side throughput tests (streaming vs batched) with same model payloads so you can measure token-cost and error-rate deltas vs hyperscalers.

Proposed tests (short list)
1) Baseline steady-state test (3 hours): 50 qps mixed online/batch to capture normal latency and error rates.
2) Burst ramp test (30m): synthetic 10x burst to observe error budget consumption and automatic throttling.
3) Region failover probe (series of 5 partial outages): validate routing to secondary region and kv-cache warmup impact on tail latency.
4) Rate-limit policy verification: intentionally exceed configured per-client RPS to validate 429 semantics and backoff headers.

Immediate asks from EdgeStream
- A list of representative endpoints/payload sizes and any auth tokens we should use for the load scripts.
- A primary contact from your infra team to coordinate the failover window (so we don't overlap with production maintenance).

Attachments included: edge-inference-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO baseline), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-appendix.pdf (short diff notes), reliability-probe-load-script.tar.gz (load harness).

Suggested owners for next steps
- Redwood: Priyom (technical lead, will own test harness), Camila (solutions PM, orchestration and dashboards), Olga (deal lead / escalation).
- EdgeStream: Ryan (product lead), Leah (infra contact).

Proposed schedule
- T+1: share any payloads / auth details (EdgeStream)
- T+2: run baseline test (Redwood / EdgeStream in collaboration)
- T+3: follow-up recap with graphs + proposed remediation if we see regressions.

If that aligns I’ll schedule the technical window Wed-Fri next week and loop in Ben for commercial alignment (credits/SLA phrasing if we need a temporary test SLA).

Thanks —
Olga

Thanks Olga — useful summary. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Rate limits: can you share the exact semantics we'll see in 429 responses? We need concrete headers to build backoff logic (eg. Retry-After vs custom backoff). Also are you able to expose per-token vs per-request limits?

2) Error budget definition: for the eval we want to treat 5xx and 429s differently — do you track those separately in the SLO spreadsheet you attached?

3) Failover window: our infra lead is in EMEA and only available Tue-Thu afternoons PST — can we aim for Thursday window?

We’ll also send a small sample of payloads (1k and 10k token-size attempts) and an API token with a test role. If you can share the load harness details, we’ll try a dry run tomorrow.

Appreciate the clarity on owners — I’ll loop in our infra contact once we confirm Thursday.

—Ryan

Subject: RE: EdgeStream evaluation: reliability probes, baseline metrics, and next tests

Hi all —

Following up with concrete numbers and the technical test plan. I pulled baseline stats from our internal staging cluster that best mirrors the Redwood hosted environment we will use for the run: 

Baseline targets (staging)
- Uptime target: 99.99% (measured monthly), observed in staging over last 30 days: 99.995%.
- Latency: online p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=180ms for 512-token requests (single-model, warm KV cache).
- Batch tail latency (1000-token batches): p95=420ms, p99=1.1s.
- Rate limiting policy (default): token-based quota per API key (tokens/sec) + concurrent-connection soft cap. When a client hits quota we return 429 with headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After (seconds). We also optionally return X-Token-Limit for token-specific throttles.
- Error classification: 5xx are server errors (counted against error budget); 429s are user-triggered throttles (separate throttle budget). We provide a combined dashboard and breakdown by error category.

Proposed test harness
- Load script (attached) will run the following scenarios: steady-state mixed traffic, 10x burst, sustained high concurrency, and region failover probes. The harness reports per-call fields (status, latency, token usage).
- For failover probes we’ll simulate progressive regional egress (20%, 50%, 100% traffic redirection) and validate routing-based fallback to secondary region; we'll capture cold-start impact on KV cache and model variant fallback rates.

Data to collect (EdgeStream / Redwood)
- Per-second error counts (5xx vs 4xx vs 429)
- Per-request latency histogram and per-client token consumption
- Observed failover time (time to route to secondary + time to restore p95 latency within 2x baseline)

Operational constraints
- We recommend running the region failover probe during a low-traffic window (EdgeStream to propose). The tests are destructive by design (intended to probe graceful degradation), so we want a single coordinated window.

Next steps (owners & timing)
- EdgeStream: provide payload samples + preferred Thursday window for failover (Ryan).
- Redwood: Priyom will run the harness, Camila will own dashboards, Olga will coordinate commercial notes and credits with Ben.

I’ll also upload the harness logs and a sample results spreadsheet to the shared Drive link once we run the baseline.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
